newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Security Council to meet Friday on Mideast violence.
newsitem.headline: Security Council to meet Friday on Mideast violence.

text.p: The Security Council will hold a formal meeting on Friday at 11 a.m. EDT (1500 gmt) on the situation in the Israeli-occupied territories, where more than 50 people have been killed in clashes between Palestinians and Israeli troops in the past two days, the president of the council said on Thursday.
The debate will be preceded by closed-door consultations, Council President Alfredo Lopes Cabral of Guinea-Bissau added.

The council meeting, announced after closed-door council consultations, was requested by Saudia Arabia, as current chairman of the Arab group at the United Nations, and by Egypt, which is a member of the Security Council.

Arab sources said the group was seeking the closing of an Israeli-excavated archaeological tunnel in the Old City of Jerusalem, near Islamic and Jewish holy places, which sparked Palestinian protest demonstrations.
It also wants the council to demand that Israel resume the Middle East peace process and abide by agreements already concluded with the Palestinian Authority, the sources said.

In a statement on Wednesday in response to a letter from the Palestine Liberation Organisation, Cabral said council members were concerned at the situation in Jerusalem and the West Bank town of Ramallah, scene of much of the initial bloodshed, and urged "all sides to move quickly to restore calm and to exercise restraint and avoid further violence."
